LibraForge matching benchmark

2026-11-02 · LibraForge 22b5c9c · Audible public catalog (no login), US marketplace, Goodreads fallback

Want a test run again (a newer version of a tool, a different setting) or another tool added to the comparison? Open an issue to re-run a test or open an issue to add a tool. Every tool is scored the same way, on the same books and with the same metrics as below.

Results · How each tool matches · All tools · Every book

4,044 audiobooks in their original state, before any matching: the tags LibraForge saved before it first wrote anything to a library's books, or another library's files as they were. Each book was matched again from those original tags, its folder path and its runtime, with no login, against the live catalog, the same way Metadata Forge matches a new book. 2,994 books have a confirmed answer (a match applied and reviewed by hand). For 998 more, not yet confirmed, a curated file name ("Author; Series; Book NN; Title") is the answer. A pick is correct when it is the right book: the same author, and the same series and number or the same title, in any recording (a US or a UK narration, a re-recording), since no tool can tell from tags which narration a file is. A translation, or a listing under half or over one and a half times the file's runtime (an abridgement, an excerpt, an omnibus), is not the book. A series-only match, which writes only the series and keeps the book's details, is correct when the series is the book's, or the one the file already carried. Only books with an answer are scored. "Held" means the tool sent its pick to review instead of applying it; a book LibraForge refused (no candidate reached its minimum score) counts as no match. 160 books the rules misjudge (a wrong library answer, a book Audible names by its subtitle, a publisher in the author's place) were reviewed by hand; each says why in its "reviewed by hand" line, and the verdict counts for every tool that picked the same listing.

Compared with other tools

Each tool got the same original tags as files carrying them (silent files at the books' real folder paths; for tools that check runtime, as long as the real book) and was scored the same way. Only LibraForge and AudioSilo hold a match for review; the others apply what they accept, so their held columns read n/a.

Why AudioSilo matched 4,044 books in about a minute

Every other tool here asks a web service for each book: every search is a round trip to Audible or Goodreads, usually a second or so and often several per book, and most tools also pause between books so the service doesn't block them. Even spread over 5 workers, that adds up to about 29 minutes for LibraForge and hours for most of the others.

AudioSilo can skip all of that. AudioSilo is part of its own metadata project (audiosilo-meta, a community database released as CC0), and in mirror mode the server downloads the whole database once: one SQLite file of about 320,000 recordings of 300,000 works (a 517 MB download, about 2 GB on disk), with a full-text search index built in, refreshed daily from GitHub. Matching a book then is a query against that file on the same disk: no network, no rate limit, nothing to wait for. That came to about 15 milliseconds per book with its 2 workers, and not a single request to their service during the run, which is kind to their servers too.

The trade-off is coverage: it can only find what the community has added, which is why more of its books land in review or no match than LibraForge's. The speed is a design choice, not a shortcut: it searched every book and checked runtime on every match.

Setup per tool

  • AudioSilo (v2.5.1): "Match automatically" over the library, in mirror mode (a local copy of the community database, so the run made no calls to their service). Confident matches count as applied, "to review" as held.
  • Audiobookshelf Quick Match (v2.35.1, Audible US provider): the Quick Match button per book, which takes the first Audible result, looked up by the file's ASIN when it has one. Run one book at a time, as ABS's own Match All does.
  • BookOrbit: a library bulk metadata fetch with its default providers.
  • beets-audible (beets 2.14, the plugin's recommended settings): beet import -q, which applies strong matches and skips the rest; skipped books count as no match. beets was given each book's real runtime, since it scores candidates on track length.
  • LibraForge: lf_bench.py over the same files, public catalog with the Goodreads fallback on, 5 search workers.
  • Grimmory (v3.5.0): a library metadata refresh with Audible enabled and first for every field (Goodreads, then Google behind it), applied without review. Per provider it takes the top result: one keyword search, first result. It reads the iTunes-atom copies of the tags, which carry no ASIN.
  • ReadMeABook (v1.2.12): the Bulk Import scan, which picks an Audible match per book by itself (one catalog search on album, album artist and composer, first result). It groups folders by their tags, so books it merged into a parent folder count as no match. Its scan returns no series.
